— Section I — Below the Flood / Dry Deep —
Ancient Siren Apothecary

The Apothecary predates any current map of the Forge Network. It exists in the dry deep zone — below the Rift Flood, below the sub-platform maintenance levels, below the unauthorized Furnace installations the Affiliates believe are their private infrastructure. It was here before any of that. It was here before the Affiliates had a name for themselves.

In the old usage, an apothecary was not merely a pharmacy — it was a knowledge repository. A place where ingredients were prepared, studied, and preserved. Where the relationship between materials and outcomes was recorded through generations of careful practice. The Ancient Siren Apothecary operates on this model at network scale: a repository of Forge Network materials, instruments, historical records, and the preserved operational artifacts of Siren practice going back to before the surface rail system existed.

The architectural crossing tells the age: classical marble columns and cracked stone floors mixed with Forge infrastructure that has grown into the space rather than been installed. The Ley line pillar at the center of the archive chambers is not a constructed support — it is a Ley line that became structural over centuries. The space was built around things that were already here. The classical elements were additions. The Forge infrastructure was original.

Grand Entrance Hall — Armillary Court
Ancient Siren Apothecary
Below Flood Level / Dry Deep / Forge Node Active / Classification: Pre-Network Record
  • ArmillaryForge Network Cartography Instrument. The armillary sphere functions as a room-scale version of the Alchemy Board — the rings represent Ley line trajectories from this node outward.   • Globe PedestalSecondary node instrument. The smaller globe on its pedestal is a single-node reader — it shows the local Forge activity of the Apothecary node only. Used for maintenance monitoring. Significantly older than the armillary sphere beside it.
  • Kaiju SkullProvenance marker. The skull mounted above the archway is from a Kaiju used as a Goblin alloy source. Preserved here as a material record. The Apothecary documents what the Forge Network's manufacturing history used. The skull is not a trophy. It is an ingredient catalogue entry.
  • Fire CircleNode stone formation hearth. The central fire ring maintains the thermal conditions under which node stones form. Stones retrieved from the deep Cenote systems are kept in this heat-active environment to preserve their formation state before integration. The fire does not consume. It maintains.
  • White StatuesSiren operational records. The classical-style figures throughout the Apothecary are not decorative. They are three-dimensional operational records of historical Siren configurations — what a Siren of a specific class looked like in active deployment. The Apothecary does not use text records for Siren configurations. It uses these.

Spatial Architecture — Known Chambers
Grand Entrance / Armillary Court
First chamber. Armillary sphere, globe pedestal, fire circle, entry statues, cracked marble floor. The bright white light quality here is Forge energy bleeding through the ceiling — the node directly above has been active for longer than the structure around it.
Archive Chamber A — Display Hall
Historical automaton specimens in illuminated preservation cases. Books (Forge Mystic texts). Kaiju skull archway leading deeper. Central Siren historical figure. Ley line structural column — twisted, dark, ancient. Sarcophagus on stone table.
Archive Chamber B — Instrument Gallery
Siren figure in active pose at center (arms raised, instrument configuration). Additional specimen cases. Node stone display bowls. An open book on the floor — left open, not abandoned. Someone was reading it recently enough that it was not shelved.
Engine Vault — Forge Substrate
The oldest chamber. The Forge engine mechanism on the rear wall is not a displayed artifact — it is functional infrastructure. The Apothecary was built AROUND this engine. It has been running continuously. The blue ceiling visible in this chamber is the flood water pressed against the outer structure — the Apothecary sits at the exact boundary where the dry deep meets the base of the Rift Flood.
West Corridor — Guardian Alcoves
Two ancient guardian golems stand in carved alcoves at the corridor junction. Stone-colored, heavy, armed with shield and weapon. They are not dormant. They are waiting. The transition from the dark industrial corridor into the bright Archive space is abrupt — the Apothecary maintains its own light environment.
Node Stone Formation Alcove
Location: Behind the engine vault. Not photographed. Contains active formation conditions — the heat from the engine creates a thermal column in which stones form over decades. The small stones visible on pedestals in the Archive chambers originate here. The Apothecary is both repository and production facility.

What the Apothecary Contains

The display cases throughout the Archive Chambers hold automaton specimens from across the network's history — units that were recovered, studied, and preserved rather than destroyed. A Forge Mystic's working library remains on the shelves (visible in Archive Chamber A), the texts undisturbed. The Siren figures throughout are not statues in the artistic sense — they are three-dimensional operational records, each one capturing a specific configuration, a specific class, a specific historical moment in Siren development.

One of the display cases (visible in Archive Chamber A, right side) holds a specimen that resembles a CST-adjacent armored unit — orange and dark, compact, fully preserved. The Apothecary predates the CST. Whatever this unit represents existed before the organization that built something like it. This is either a coincidence of design convergence or evidence that the CST's engineering drew from Apothecary records at some point in its institutional history. The Apothecary does not distinguish. It keeps everything.

Narrative function: The Apothecary is the first place Brae can encounter the full scope of what a Siren is, was, and can become — in historical form, without the network demanding she act on it immediately. This is the one location in the story that is patient. It is not a threat space. It is a reading room. What she chooses to read here shapes what kind of Siren she becomes.
Connection to the open book: The book on the floor of Archive Chamber B was left open by someone. The Apothecary predates all current factions. If someone has been here recently enough to leave a book open, either the network has been sending white cells here for longer than anyone understands, or someone else found access. The Steamfitters are the only other faction with the kind of deep-network knowledge that could locate this space. Or the book has been open for three hundred years and no one has moved it. Both readings are valid. Keep both open.
— Section II — Siren Navigation & Cartography —
Siren Alchemy Boards
Alchemy Boards (Blank & Active) + Ley Line Extraction Station
Siren Cartographic Instrument — Personal Network Map
Siren Alchemy Boards
Classification: Navigation / Cartography / Ley Line Interface
Node Stone Integration: Required for activation
Found: Apothecary Archive / Siren operational kit

The Alchemy Board is a Siren's personal map of the Forge Network — not a fixed cartographic document but a dynamic instrument that updates in real time based on the bonded Siren's Core frequency and position. It does not show the whole network. No instrument does. It shows the network as perceived from the Siren's current node position, extending outward as far as their Core sensitivity reaches.

The board is shaped to be carried — the curved base locks into a Siren's harness, the body extending behind them in a configuration that keeps both hands free while the board continuously reads and displays. In combat configuration it is carried at angle, the active face visible to the Siren during movement.

Unactivated State
Blank Board
Cream-white surface. The engravings are present but dormant — the Forge script is inscribed into the board material but carries no light because no Core has bonded it. This is the board as it exists in the Apothecary display cases. A potential map, not yet a map. The node stone insets are present, flush with the surface, waiting for a frequency to resonate with.
Activated State
Active Board
Dark surface. The Forge script illuminated from within — teal, gold, and red insets glowing at active node positions. The concentric circle map at the center shows the network as perceived from the bonded Siren's current position. The red markers: threat signatures. The teal markers: active Forge nodes. The gold: Ley line primary routes. The branching lines extending outward grow or recede as the Siren moves through the network.

The Ley Line Extraction Station

The alchemical workstation visible to the right of the boards is a Ley line extraction instrument — a Siren-operated apparatus for isolating, sampling, and containing discrete sections of Forge Network Ley line energy for study and application. The teal glowing container on the workstation holds a captured Ley line fragment in containment: Forge energy removed from its natural channel and stabilized for examination.

The dragon-form coiling around the workstation is what a Ley line looks like when it is being contained rather than flowing freely. Unimpeded Ley line energy moves as light through the network substrate — invisible to most, visible as a golden river to Siren perception. When it is extracted from its channel and forced into containment, the energy adopts the shape of its compression. The coiling, serpentine form is not creature anatomy. It is what pressure does to a current. The Ley line is reacting to being held.

Story implication: The Ley Line Extraction Station at the Apothecary is intact and functional. Siren alchemy — the practice of working with extracted Ley line fragments to produce specific effects — is a capability Brae has not yet discovered. The boards in the Apothecary are unactivated, waiting. The workstation has been used, the instruments arranged mid-process. Someone left them that way. The Apothecary is not only a repository. It is a laboratory that is still in use.
— Section III — CST Special Operations —
Siren Witch Hunter Unit
CST Special Operations — Witch Hunter Designation — Station City
CST Special Operations — Witch Hunter Designation
Ghostface Assassin Golem
Designation: Witch Hunter / Anti-Siren Specialist
Signal Core: Blue — CST Operational Frequency
Location: Station City / Southern Line deployment
Weapon: Resonance Staff — Core Disruption Class

Lyra, Rael, and Torch are line CST — gantry team, standard deployment, operational authority within a station's jurisdiction. The Ghostface Golem is above that tier. This is CST Special Operations: the unit type that deploys when a situation has produced Glitch Witches and the standard gantry team cannot contain them.

The blue chest core is the defining distinction. It is not Forge amber. It is not Affiliate contamination green. It is CST's own operational frequency — a signal derived from Forge Network-adjacent technology but maintained and calibrated independently by the organization. A Witch's corrupted perception cannot lock onto a blue core the way it locks onto Forge-origin signals. The Ghostface Golem is engineered to be something a Witch's broken targeting system resolves incorrectly.

The hood and concealed face serve the same purpose at close range: a Witch that cannot resolve a face cannot lock its corrupted targeting on the individual. The Ghostface Golem is designed to approach a Witch in a state where the Witch's own broken perception cannot correctly assess the threat. By the time the Witch resolves what it is looking at, the resonance staff has already been brought to range.

The Resonance Staff

The gothic-ornate staff weapon is a Core disruption instrument — not a cutting weapon but a frequency weapon. When brought to range of a damaged node stone Core, the staff emits a resonance pattern that interferes with the broken signal a Glitch Witch is running on. It does not destroy the Core. It interrupts the corrupted signal long enough to create a window in the Witch's coherence. What is done with that window is the Witch Hunter's tactical decision.

The distinction from standard CST: Lyra's unit can observe a Witch and survive. They cannot reliably neutralize one without significant cost. The Ghostface Golem is deployed specifically when neutralization is the objective. Station City maintains a standing number of these units because the Witch Commander's organized network means organized Witch activity is now a southern-line operational reality rather than an isolated incident response.

Tactical implication: The Witch Commander receives the Gateway contamination signal. She can broadcast it. The Witch Hunter's blue core is specifically designed to be unresolvable to a Witch operating on Gateway contamination frequency. But the Witch Commander is not a standard Witch — she receives both the broken Forge signal AND the Gateway signal simultaneously. Whether the blue core is truly unresolvable to her is an open question. The first time a Ghostface Golem encounters the Witch Commander is a scene that needs to be written.
— Section IV — Steamfitters Guild — Aerial Survey —
Tengu Golem Combat Armor
Steamfitters Guild — Tengu Designation — Station City Deployment
Steamfitters Guild — Aerial Survey & Combat Platform
Tengu Golem Armor
Designation: Tengu — Aerial Survey / Senior Combat
Signal Core: Red-Orange — Elevated Steamfitter Designation
Location: Station City elevated positions
Wings: Structural / Powered flight capable

The Steamfitters' standard Rare Combat Automaton (seen in the Malvek Dossier) operates at ground level on the calibration platforms. The Tengu designation goes higher. These units are deployed to the elevated positions above Station City's tower structure — the spires, the upper transit bridges, the roof architecture that the fog covers at ground level but that stands clear above it.

The wings are not decorative and not a design flourish from the Tengu mythological reference. They are structural flight appendages: the Steamfitters' engineering integrates actual load-bearing aerial capability into senior unit construction. A Tengu can reach positions that no surface automaton reaches. In Station City's density — where towers are so close that the space between them is effectively another surface — Tengu units move through the structure the way birds move through a forest.

Aerial Survey Function

The primary Tengu role at Station City is network corruption mapping from elevation. The Steamfitters have known the southern Forge Network is degrading for longer than any other faction — their calibration instruments at Metro Center registered the corruption patterns before the Affiliates named themselves. What they have been unable to do from ground level is triangulate the corruption's source and spread with precision. The Tengu units, operating from Station City's upper reaches, can triangulate from three or four elevated positions simultaneously.

The chest disc — a miniaturized version of the calibration wheel in the ground-level Rare unit's background — is the elevation-survey instrument. From height, with clear Ley line visibility above the fog, the disc reads the network's energy signature across a wide arc and compares it against the baseline record the Steamfitters have maintained for generations. The deviation map this produces is the most accurate record of the Affiliate corruption's scope available from any faction.

The red-orange eye cores: Standard Steamfitter Rare units carry amber optics. The red-orange cores on a Tengu designation indicate elevated operational authority — this unit has priority access to the Steamfitters' senior calibration network. What it observes goes directly to the senior guild calibrators. Not filtered through field reporting chains. Directly. The Steamfitters treat Tengu data as their most reliable intelligence source.
Story placement: The previous Steamfitter entry (Rare Combat Automaton) was positioned at a calibration platform at Station City — the Steamfitters watching the southern degradation from Metro Center. The Tengu is the instrument doing the watching. This is the unit that produced the data that placed the Rare Automaton at that calibration platform. If Brae reaches Station City and makes contact with the Steamfitters, the Tengu is how she finds out what the Affiliates have actually done to the network — not a partial picture from a single station, but the full arc of the corruption as seen from above it.
The open question between factions: The Ghostface Witch Hunter is CST's response to the Witch situation. The Tengu is the Steamfitters' response to the network corruption situation. Both factions are independently tracking the same problem from different angles — CST through the operational damage (Witches on the line), Steamfitters through the network damage (Ley line degradation). Neither faction has shared data with the other. Neither faction knows the other has data. Brae is positioned to be the point of connection between these two independent bodies of knowledge. Whether she does so by design, by accident, or because the network routes her that way is the structural choice for Act Two.
